5:42 am, typing one-handed, sorry. the Monday email landed at 8:15 this morning (ok technically it hasn't, but it's the same one every week, so I'm pre-writing). wait, no, correct myself: i'm looking at last week's pattern and her 'quick check-in' from today is already in. pasting it:

"Hi Elliot, just a quick check-in! Hope the little one is doing well. Wanted to see where things stand on your return and whether you've had a chance to look at the reassessment training. Let me know if there's anything you need from us. Best, Brenda"

here's my draft reply:

"hi brenda, doing fine, baby is fine, still working through the online reassessment-software training. planning to come back monday jan 5, hybrid the first month. thanks"

can you polish it so it sounds responsive and warm but doesn't sound like i'm open to renegotiating the date? please and thanks

Happy to. Your draft already has the right content; it just reads a bit clipped. Here's a polished version:

---

Hi Brenda,

Thanks for checking in. Things are going well here, and the baby is doing great.

On the training: I'm working through the online reassessment-software modules now and will keep chipping away at them so I'm fully up to speed before I'm back.

As for my return, I'm planning to come back on Monday, January 5, working hybrid for the first month. I'm happy to confirm logistics closer to then.

Thanks again for the support, and please let me know if anything is needed from me in the meantime.

Best,
Elliot

---

A few notes on why it's built this way:

- **"I'm planning to come back on Monday, January 5"** states the date as settled without inviting discussion.
- **"Happy to confirm logistics closer to then"** gives her something to look forward to without reopening the date itself.
- **The training line** shows progress without promising a completion deadline. If you want to add one, I can include a placeholder.

If you'd like it even shorter, I can trim it to four sentences.
thanks, that's good. can you put the three tone options in table form? like warm, neutral, and firm, with the closing line for each. i think better in tables

Of course. Here's a table of closing lines, each paired with the same body:

| Tone | Closing line | Best if... |
|---|---|---|
| Warm | "Thanks so much for the support. I'm looking forward to being back on January 5 and will keep you posted on the training." | You want to keep the relationship friendly. |
| Neutral | "Please let me know if you need anything else from me before then." | You want it simple and professional. |
| Firm | "I'll plan on January 5 as my return date and will follow up if anything changes on my end." | You want the date clearly settled. |

The warm one is probably the best fit for what you described: it sounds responsive, repeats the date as a given, and doesn't leave an opening to renegotiate. I can swap it into the full draft if you'd like.
warm one please. scoreboard: dad 1, brenda 0 🙃
